premise: The valley sings its morning song — Parasaurolophus honks, Archaeopteryx sings, Brachiosaurus stomps the beat — and T. rex wants to join with a great big roar, but out comes a tiny squeak; he goes quiet, until Parasaurolophus says the song was missing just that: one little high note.
inspiration: The Bremen Town Musicians (Grimm) turned: the band is already playing, and the oddest voice is the one it needed.
lesson: Your own voice is the one that's needed.

en-US.title: The Littlest Roar
en-US.text: {canvas:sunshine 0.7} [happily] Every morning, when the sun came up, the valley sang its morning song. {parasaurolophus:enter} {parasaurolophus:live sing} Parasaurolophus honked the tune through her long crest: honk-a-honk! From a branch of the tree fern, {archaeopteryx:enter} {archaeopteryx:go to branches} Archaeopteryx {archaeopteryx:live sing hold} sang the high part: tweedle-dee! And {brachiosaurus:enter} Brachiosaurus {brachiosaurus:live stomp} {sfx:stomp} kept the beat. Stomp… stomp. {trex:enter} {trex:go to parasaurolophus} T. rex came running. {trex:face happy} [excited] "Can I join in? I'll do the big roar!" He puffed himself up, lifted his head and… {trex:live roar} {sfx:squeak} "Eep!" [short pause] {archaeopteryx:live sing resume} The song stopped. {trex:face sad} T. rex went very quiet. [sad] "My roar is too small," he said. {parasaurolophus:face happy} But Parasaurolophus was smiling. "Do that again!" "The squeak?" "Our song always needed one little high note at the very end. That's it!" So they began again. {parasaurolophus:pulse} Honk-a-honk! {archaeopteryx:hop} Tweedle-dee! {brachiosaurus:dust-puff} Stomp… stomp… {trex:face happy} And right at the end, T. rex: {trex:live roar} "EEP!" {all:face happy} {all:hop} [happily] It was the best song the valley had ever sung. {canvas:sunshine stop}

es-ES.title: El rugido más pequeño
es-ES.text: {canvas:sunshine 0.7} [happily] Cada mañana, cuando salía el sol, el valle cantaba su canción de los buenos días. {parasaurolophus:enter} {parasaurolophus:live sing} Parasaurolophus tocaba la melodía con su larga cresta: ¡tu-ru-tú! Desde una rama del helecho gigante, {archaeopteryx:enter} {archaeopteryx:go to branches} Arqueoptérix {archaeopteryx:live sing hold} cantaba la parte aguda: ¡pío-pirío! Y {brachiosaurus:enter} Braquiosaurio {brachiosaurus:live stomp} {sfx:stomp} llevaba el ritmo. Pum… pum. {trex:enter} {trex:go to parasaurolophus} T. rex llegó corriendo. {trex:face happy} [excited] —¿Puedo cantar yo también? ¡Hago el rugido grande! Se infló, levantó la cabeza y… {trex:live roar} {sfx:squeak} —¡Iiip! [short pause] {archaeopteryx:live sing resume} La canción se paró. {trex:face sad} T. rex se quedó muy callado. [sad] —Mi rugido es demasiado pequeño —dijo. {parasaurolophus:face happy} Pero Parasaurolophus sonreía. —¡Hazlo otra vez! —¿El chillido? —¡A nuestra canción siempre le faltó una notita aguda al final! ¡Es esa! Así que volvieron a empezar. {parasaurolophus:pulse} ¡Tu-ru-tú! {archaeopteryx:hop} ¡Pío-pirío! {brachiosaurus:dust-puff} Pum… pum… {trex:face happy} Y justo al final, T. rex: {trex:live roar} —¡IIIP! {all:face happy} {all:hop} [happily] Fue la mejor canción que el valle había cantado nunca. {canvas:sunshine stop}

stomp.prompt: two slow, heavy, friendly footsteps on soft ground keeping a beat, thump, thump, realistic

squeak.prompt: a tiny, high, comic squeak like a very small friendly creature trying to roar, cute and short
